works.title: Uisang · Diagram of the Dharma Realm
works.body: A poem arranged as a seal-diagram. Uisang’s Ocean Seal brings text, image, recitation and the interpenetration of all things into one work.

works.title: Jikji · Pointing Directly to Mind
works.body: A Korean Buddhist work on mind and awakening. Its 1377 edition is the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type.

works.title: Zhuangzi · Cook Ding
works.body: Practiced movement and cultivated attention. Bring the butcher’s account into conversation with music and sport.

works.title: Turing · Computing Machinery and Intelligence
works.body: A concrete text for examining how we recognize thinking in a machine.

works.title: Oliveros · Sonic Meditations
works.body: Text scores make attention and collective listening part of the musical work itself.

works.title: Dhammapada · Verses on mind
works.body: Mental cultivation, attention and conduct within a Buddhist account of liberation.

works.title: Dickinson · The Brain—is wider than the Sky—
works.body: A short poem makes mind, world and scale available through the precision of poetic form.

works.title: Dickinson · I felt a Cleaving in my Mind—
works.body: Division, sequence and the effort to reconnect thought. A compact work for close attention to language.

works.title: Dickinson · I felt a Funeral, in my Brain,
works.body: Sound, movement and the breakdown of sense make an inward experience take poetic form.

works.title: Zhuangzi · The butterfly dream
works.body: Dreaming, transformation and the limits of a fixed account of self.

works.title: Borges · Funes, His Memory
works.body: A person who cannot forget makes perfect memory a problem for thinking.

works.title: Du Bois · The Souls of Black Folk
works.body: Double-consciousness, racial power and the social self. The Sorrow Songs make listening part of reading.

works.title: Hyecho · A Buddhist pilgrimage account
works.body: Observation, interpretation and religious life across cultures. Korean Buddhist translation expertise belongs in this conversation.

works.title: Deliverance from Error
works.body: An autobiographical search for reliable knowledge, from radical doubt to religious practice.

works.title: Kokoro
works.body: Trust, guilt and the difficulty of knowing another person. The title itself joins heart and mind.

works.title: The Lathe of Heaven
works.body: Dreams alter reality; a supposed cure becomes a struggle over whose imagined world others must inhabit.

works.title: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
works.body: Recognition, memory and identity through accounts of people living with neurological differences.

works.title: Gregorian chant
works.body: Breath, memorization, collective attention and acoustic space. Select a named chant and recording with a music specialist.

works.title: Caminhando / Walking
works.body: An artwork unfolds through a participant’s action: cutting a paper Möbius strip makes choice and perception part of its form.

thinkers.title: Michael Levin
thinkers.body: Cellular communication and collective problem-solving broaden the study of cognition. Adaptive behavior and felt experience remain distinct claims.

thinkers.title: Mark Solms
thinkers.body: An account of consciousness that places feeling and bodily needs at its center. Begin with The Hidden Spring, then examine the research.

thinkers.title: Cameron Berg
thinkers.body: Work on artificial systems, learning and reports of experience. Examine what the experiments establish and what remains an interpretation.

thinkers.title: Uisang / Ŭisang
thinkers.body: The Ocean Seal gives philosophical thought a visual and recitable form. Its Buddhist account of interpenetration belongs beside the poem’s patterned design.

thinkers.title: Zhuangzi
thinkers.body: Dreams, skilled action and shifting perspectives unsettle a fixed account of the knowing self.

thinkers.title: Emily Dickinson
thinkers.body: The brain, the sky, a funeral, a cleaving: poems use exact language to make thought and its disruptions perceptible.

thinkers.title: Al-Ghazālī
thinkers.body: Examines the limits of perception and reasoning within an account of religious knowledge and practice.

thinkers.title: W. E. B. Du Bois
thinkers.body: Double-consciousness describes self-understanding under racial domination. The social world enters the experience of being a person.

thinkers.title: Pauline Oliveros
thinkers.body: Makes attention, listening and participation material for musical work. Sonic Meditations offers a concrete place to begin.

thinkers.title: Alan Turing
thinkers.body: Turns judgments about machine thinking into an explicit test. His essay gives AI discussions a shared text and a history.

thinkers.title: William James
thinkers.body: The stream of thought, attention and habit connect everyday experience with the early development of psychology.

thinkers.title: Anton Wilhelm Amo
thinkers.body: An African philosopher working in eighteenth-century Europe contests the attribution of sensation to the mind.

concepts.title: Consciousness
concepts.body: Having an experience, such as pain or seeing color. Distinguish this from solving a problem or producing a convincing verbal report.

concepts.title: Placebo / nocebo
concepts.body: The contexts and expectations surrounding treatment can affect symptoms and experience. Changes in symptoms are not a universal cure.

concepts.title: Animism
concepts.body: Relationships with animals, places and other beings understood as persons or agents. Specific communities and traditions must lead the comparison.

concepts.title: Panpsychism
concepts.body: Philosophical views that make mentality or experience fundamental and widespread in nature. Distinct from animism and from the claim that everything thinks like a human.

concepts.title: Self / soul / person
concepts.body: These terms name different problems across traditions: the owner of experience, a life’s continuity, spiritual existence and social recognition.

concepts.title: Heart-mind
concepts.body: 心, 마음 and other words connect aspects of feeling, intention and thought. Their meanings overlap without becoming interchangeable.

concepts.title: Memory
concepts.body: Remembering sustains knowledge and a sense of self. Funes makes total recall troubling; learning a poem makes memory tangible.

concepts.title: Embodied & distributed cognition
concepts.body: Thinking can depend on bodily action, gesture, material tools and social coordination. Hands and surroundings can participate in the work of thought.

concepts.title: Attention & skilled action
concepts.body: Selection and practice shape what becomes available to thought and action. Cook Ding, singing and sport bring skilled movement into view.

concepts.title: Chant & collective trance
concepts.body: Rhythm, repetition and movement can organize shared experience. Chant and trance are not synonyms; study named practices in their settings.

concepts.title: Double-consciousness
concepts.body: Du Bois describes the tension of knowing oneself through a society that devalues one’s personhood. This is a historically specific account of the social self.

concepts.title: Artificial minds
concepts.body: What makes a mind “real”? Performance, subjective experience, agency and moral standing need separate examination.

faculty.title: Mark Phelan
faculty.body: Researches philosophy of mind and how mental states are attributed. His public lecture Knowing Others and Ourselves offers a campus starting point.
faculty.connection: AI, other minds and the evidence behind attributing consciousness.

faculty.title: Chunyue Teng
faculty.body: Studies visual attention, working memory and cognitive control using EEG, behavioral measures and computational models.
faculty.connection: Perception, memory and the experimental study of mind.

faculty.title: Karen Leigh-Post
faculty.body: Author of Mind-Body Awareness for Singers; applies cognitive neuroscience and perceptual-motor research to vocal performance.
faculty.connection: A work that directly joins mind, body and musical practice.

faculty.title: Julie McQuinn
faculty.body: Teaches music and memory, music and disability, opera and film music. Her research addresses music, identity and meaning.
faculty.connection: Memory, identity and the ways music shapes experience.

faculty.title: Sonja Lynn Downing
faculty.body: Studies Balinese gamelan, dance and musical learning. Author of Gamelan Girls.
faculty.connection: Embodied learning, ensemble coordination and cultural context.

faculty.title: Bob Williams
faculty.body: Studies gesture, collaborative reasoning and how people construct meaning in interaction.
faculty.connection: Mind in the hands; thinking with people, objects and gestures.

faculty.title: Melissa H. Range
faculty.body: Teaches poetry and nineteenth-century American literature, with emphasis on women writers and writers of color.
faculty.connection: Dickinson, the language of inward experience and memorization.

faculty.title: Matty Wegehaupt
faculty.body: Teaches East Asian cultures and religions; contributed to the translation of Hyecho’s travel records and has translated Beopjeong.
faculty.connection: Korean Buddhist texts, Uisang, Jikji and mind across languages.

faculty.title: Martyn Smith
faculty.body: Studies religion, place and shared meaning; teaches Islam, religion and ecology, and religion and technology.
faculty.connection: Religious accounts of self and the worlds communities inhabit.

faculty.title: Kuo-ming Sung
faculty.body: Professor of Chinese and Linguistics, with training in Romance linguistics.
faculty.connection: Comparative language, translation and the vocabulary of mind.

faculty.title: Benjamin Rinehart
faculty.body: Makes socially engaged prints, books and movable works that invite physical and psychological interaction.
faculty.connection: Jikji, the artist’s book, perception and participatory art.
